incoming.name: Invasive species
incoming.excerpt: Examples of this are the introductions of the amethyst gem clam (Gemma gemma) and the European green crab (Carcinus maenas).

outgoing.name: 19th century
outgoing.excerpt: In Australia, C. maenas was first reported in the late 19th century, in Port Phillip Bay, Victoria.

outgoing.name: Australia
outgoing.excerpt: In Australia and New Zealand, it is referred to as either the European green crab or European shore crab.

outgoing.name: British Isles
outgoing.excerpt: In the British Isles, it is generally referred to simply as the shore crab.

outgoing.name: California
outgoing.excerpt: In 1989, C. maenas was found in San Francisco Bay, California, on the Pacific coast of the United States.

outgoing.name: Cape Town
outgoing.excerpt: C. maenas first reached South Africa in 1983, in the Table Docks area near Cape Town .
